sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A Fijian acacia described from its type specimen as a spreading tree up to 6 m tall. The type was collected on the ridge of Mount Numbuiloa on Vanua Levu at about 500–590 m. Kew records a wet tropical biome; a regional forestry paper describes the species as uncommon and known from the mountain area. Its flowers have bright yellow petals and stamens. The illustrated branch is broadly consistent with an acacia, but the available sources do not verify this exact plate as the species.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The sources consulted do not establish food uses or toxicity for this species.
